children: Malaysia's central bank is expected to leave its benchmark policy rate unchanged at 2.75% on Thursday, according to seven economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. Given subdued domestic inflation, mixed sectoral growth momentum and continued volatility in global financial markets, Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to remain cautious and data-dependent, say UOB economists Julia Goh and Jasrine Loke. The central bank is expected to stand pat while monitoring external developments closely, they say in a note. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
